# Summary 

Here we conduct an Area of Applicability (AOA) analysis on the temporal variables in our data. This is to see if the hindcast years (e.g., 1950-2014) values fall within the range of the training years, and are appropriate to use for this modelling. 

## Environment

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

rm(list = ls())

library(tidyverse)
library(qs)
library(here)
library(terra)
library(glue)
library(strex)
library(CAST)
library(janitor)
library(countrycode)
library(data.table)

source(here("R/dir.R"))

## these don't change across training and prediciton data:
global_grid <- read.csv(here("data/model_features/deg_1_x_1/global_grid.csv"))

spatial_data <- global_grid %>%
    left_join(read.csv(here("data/model_features/deg_1_x_1/gfw_static_spatial_measures.csv")) %>% dplyr::select(-lat, -lon), by = "pixel_id") %>%
   left_join(read.csv(here("data/model_features/deg_1_x_1/mesopelagiczones/mesopelagiczones_fixed.csv")), by = "pixel_id") %>%
   left_join(read.csv(here("data/model_features/deg_1_x_1/eez/eez_fix.csv")), by = "pixel_id") %>%
   left_join(read.csv(here("data/model_features/deg_1_x_1/fao/fao_fixed.csv")), by = "pixel_id") %>%
   left_join(read.csv(here("data/model_features/deg_1_x_1/oceans_fixed.csv")), by = "pixel_id") %>%
    left_join(read.csv(here("data/model_features/deg_1_x_1/seamounts.csv")), by = "pixel_id")

  gfw_reception_data <- read.csv(here("data/model_features/deg_1_x_1/gfw_reception_quality.csv"))
```

Let's do a step by step run through example with Australia for industrial fisheries.

We need:
1. Final fitted model: The ranger object for AUS, industrial, Stage 1 (the final model trained on the full dataset).
2. Training data: The exact data frame passed to ranger() for that final model, 2015–2024. The FULL DATASET (not the 60/40 split).
3. Historical prediction data: The exact data frame passed to predict() for that model, 1950–2014.
4. Allocated effort: Final AUS industrial effort by pixel_id × year, 1950–2014. The FINAL allocated effort, even after the eez constraint and such. 
5. Grid: global_grid.csv (pixel_id, lon, lat)
6. Fleet strata (Step 11): Rousseau AUS effort by year × gear × length, and the gear × length combinations present in AUS training data


```{r}
flag           <- "AUS"
hindcast_years <- 1950:2014            # industrial training = 2015-2024

stage_1_model_dir <- file.path(rdsi_dir, "prep/random_forest/stage_1_models")   # final full-data models (v2 folder if you used one)
stage_2_model_dir <- file.path(rdsi_dir, "prep/random_forest/stage_2_models")
stage_1_pred_dir  <- file.path(rdsi_dir, "prep/random_forest/predictions_all/yearly")
stage_2_pred_dir  <- file.path(rdsi_dir, "prep/random_forest/predictions_all/yearly")

effort_path <- file.path(rdsi_dir, "prep/random_forest/zenodo_data/mapped_industrial_effort_predictions_1950_2017.csv")   # FINAL constrained effort
grid_path   <- here("data/model_features/deg_1_x_1/global_grid.csv")


out_dir <- file.path(rdsi_dir, "prep/aoa/industrial")

# predictors NOT used in the AOA (each handled separately in the text):
#  - year: pre-2015 years are outside the training range by definition; at every year
#    split they follow the same branch as 2015 (other predictors still use all years; see Step 10)
#  - AIS reception: observation-process covariates
#  - categorical / ID variables: no meaningful distance (fleet strata checked in Step 9)
excl_vars <- c("year",
               "ais_reception_positions_per_day_class_A",
               "ais_reception_positions_per_day_class_B",
               "gear", "length_category",
               "eez_id", "fao_id", "meso_id", "ocean",
               "eez_region_world_bank_7", "gov_score")



# ---- helper functions ---------------------------------------------------------

read_final_model <- function(dir, stage, flag) {
  f <- list.files(dir, pattern = glue("^stage_{stage}_rf_model_full_data_{flag}_\\d+\\.qs$"), full.names = TRUE)
  if (length(f) != 1) stop("Expected 1 final model file for stage ", stage, " ", flag, ", found ", length(f))
  qs::qread(f)
} ## reads models 

# numeric, non-excluded predictors that the model actually retained
get_aoa_vars <- function(rf, train, excl_vars) {
  cand <- setdiff(rf$forest$independent.variable.names, excl_vars)
  cand[vapply(train[cand], is.numeric, logical(1))]
} ## grabs appropriate variables



# historical predictor rows, collapsed to pixel x year (gear/length strata share predictor values).
# The saved prediction files don't carry all predictors, so we take the pixel-years from the files
# (these are the cells that were actually predicted on) and join the predictors back from the SAME
# historical table used to build full_data in the prediction script (joined there by lon, lat, year).
read_preds <- function(pred_dir, flag, yrs, vars, hist_env) {
  keys <- map_dfr(yrs, \(yr) {
    f <- file.path(pred_dir, glue("model_preds_{flag}_{yr}.qs"))
    if (!file.exists(f)) return(NULL)
    qs::qread(f) %>% distinct(pixel_id, lon, lat, year)
  })

  out <- keys %>%
    left_join(hist_env %>%
                filter(year %in% yrs) %>%
                select(lon, lat, year, all_of(vars)) %>%
                distinct(),
              by = c("lon", "lat", "year"))

  n_na <- sum(!complete.cases(out[vars]))
  if (n_na > 0) warning(n_na, " predicted pixel-years have missing predictors after the join; check hist_env matches the prediction script")
  if (anyDuplicated(out[c("pixel_id", "year")])) warning("join produced duplicate pixel-years; hist_env is not unique by lon/lat/year")
  out
}


# full predictor rows for re-prediction (Step 10): saved file + any predictors it lacks
read_full_pred_rows <- function(pred_dir, flag, yr, hist_env) {
  d <- qs::qread(file.path(pred_dir, glue("model_preds_{flag}_{yr}.qs")))
  missing <- setdiff(names(hist_env), names(d))
  d %>% left_join(hist_env %>% filter(year == yr) %>% select(lon, lat, year, all_of(missing)) %>% distinct(),
                  by = c("lon", "lat", "year"))
}

# max_train_per_year: subsample training pixel-years within each year (keeps every year for the
# leave-one-year-out threshold). trainDI cost grows ~quadratically with training rows, so large
# Stage 1 training sets need this. Inf = use all rows.
run_aoa <- function(rf, train, newdata, aoa_vars, label, max_train_per_year = Inf, seed = 123) {
  imp <- rf$variable.importance[aoa_vars]
  if (is.null(imp) || anyNA(imp)) stop(label, ": missing variable importance in final model")
  imp[imp < 0] <- 0

  tr <- train   %>% select(pixel_id, year, all_of(aoa_vars)) %>% drop_na() %>% distinct()
  nd <- newdata %>% select(pixel_id, year, all_of(aoa_vars)) %>% drop_na() %>% distinct()

  if (is.finite(max_train_per_year)) {
    set.seed(seed)
    tr <- tr %>%
      group_by(year) %>%
      slice_sample(n = max_train_per_year) %>%   # groups smaller than n keep all rows
      ungroup()
  }

  if (anyDuplicated(tr[c("pixel_id", "year")])) warning(label, ": training rows not unique by pixel-year")
  if (anyDuplicated(nd[c("pixel_id", "year")])) warning(label, ": historical rows not unique by pixel-year")

  message(label, ": ", nrow(tr), " training pixel-years, ", nrow(nd), " historical pixel-years")

  tdi <- trainDI(train     = tr[, aoa_vars],
                 weight    = as.data.frame(t(imp)),
                 CVtest    = as.integer(factor(tr$year)),   # leave-one-year-out threshold
                 algorithm = "kd_tree")

  a <- aoa(newdata = nd[, aoa_vars], trainDI = tdi, algorithm = "kd_tree")

  list(vars      = aoa_vars,
       weights   = imp,
       threshold = tdi$threshold,
       bench     = tr %>% select(pixel_id, year) %>%
                     mutate(DI = tdi$trainDI, in_aoa = DI <= tdi$threshold),
       hist      = nd %>% select(pixel_id, year) %>%
                     mutate(DI = a$DI, in_aoa = a$AOA == 1),
       train_vals = tr,
       hist_vals  = nd)
}

 # function for running aoa analysis


# ---- Step 1: grab final models ------------------------------------------------------

rf_s1 <- read_final_model(stage_1_model_dir, 1, flag)
rf_s2 <- read_final_model(stage_2_model_dir, 2, flag)

rf_s1$forest$independent.variable.names
rf_s2$forest$independent.variable.names
sort(rf_s1$variable.importance, decreasing = TRUE)
sort(rf_s2$variable.importance, decreasing = TRUE) # looks good

# ---- Step 2: training data (full data, as passed to the final models) -----------
# Mirrors the final-model script, but keeps pixel_id for de-duplication and joins.

model_data_flag <- model_data_train %>%
  dplyr::select(lon, lat, flag_fin, gear, length_category, year, presence) %>%
  filter(flag_fin == flag)

distinct_cats <- model_data_flag %>% distinct(year, flag_fin, gear, length_category)

train_s1 <- tidyr::crossing(env_grid_train, distinct_cats) %>%
  left_join(env_data_train, by = c("lon", "lat", "year")) %>%
  left_join(model_data_flag, by = c("lon", "lat", "year", "flag_fin", "gear", "length_category")) %>%
  left_join(gfw_reception_data) %>%
  mutate(presence = ifelse(is.na(presence), 0, presence)) %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  distinct() # this is a recreation of the training data we used

# Stage 2 trained only where effort > 0, i.e. the presence == 1 rows of the same grid
train_s2 <- train_s1 %>% filter(presence == 1)

# both should be TRUE. If Stage 2 is FALSE, rebuild train_s2 from the Stage 2 script (keeping pixel_id)
c(stage1 = nrow(train_s1) == rf_s1$num.samples,
  stage2 = nrow(train_s2) == rf_s2$num.samples)
c(train_s1 = nrow(train_s1), model_s1 = rf_s1$num.samples,
  train_s2 = nrow(train_s2), model_s2 = rf_s2$num.samples)

range(train_s1$year)   # 2015 2024



# ---- Step 3: AOA predictors + fill-value check ------------------------------------

aoa_vars_s1 <- get_aoa_vars(rf_s1, train_s1, excl_vars)
aoa_vars_s2 <- get_aoa_vars(rf_s2, train_s2, excl_vars)
aoa_vars_s1
aoa_vars_s2

# share of exact zeros: large shares in sst/chl _sd usually mean NA was filled with 0
train_s1 %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(union(aoa_vars_s1, aoa_vars_s2)), ~ mean(.x == 0, na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "var", values_to = "share_zero") %>%
  arrange(desc(share_zero)) # ok looks fine. We did do a little bit of gapfilling but this looks OK. SST could in theory be 0 in places.


# ---- Step 4: historical predictor rows (from the saved prediction files) ----------

# hist_env = the historical predictor table joined onto full_data in your prediction script
# (env_data_fishing_areas, renamed env_data_fishing_areas_hist), including factor encoding.
hist_env <- env_data_fishing_areas_hist

hist_s1 <- read_preds(stage_1_pred_dir, flag, hindcast_years, aoa_vars_s1, hist_env)
hist_s2 <- read_preds(stage_2_pred_dir, flag, hindcast_years, aoa_vars_s2, hist_env)

range(hist_s1$year); n_distinct(hist_s1$year)
range(hist_s2$year); n_distinct(hist_s2$year)


# ---- Step 5: run the AOA ------------------------------------------------------------
# Tip: test on a few years first, e.g. filter(hist_s1, year %in% c(1950, 1980, 2010))

# Stage 1 trains on the global grid (~46k pixel-years per year), so subsample it.
# First time a small run to see how trainDI scales on your machine, e.g.:
#   system.time(run_aoa(rf_s1, train_s1, filter(hist_s1, year == 1980), aoa_vars_s1, "test", max_train_per_year = 1000))
#   system.time(run_aoa(rf_s1, train_s1, filter(hist_s1, year == 1980), aoa_vars_s1, "test", max_train_per_year = 2000))
# (roughly 4x the time for 2x the rows means quadratic scaling)
tic()
aoa_s1 <- run_aoa(rf_s1, train_s1, hist_s1, aoa_vars_s1, "AUS industrial stage 1", max_train_per_year = 5000)
toc()

tic()
aoa_s2 <- run_aoa(rf_s2, train_s2, hist_s2, aoa_vars_s2, "AUS industrial stage 2")   # small; use all rows
toc()

# Sensitivity of Stage 1 to the subsample size (report in SI): % in AOA should barely change
tic()
aoa_s1_b <- run_aoa(rf_s1, train_s1, hist_s1, aoa_vars_s1, "AUS stage 1 (n = 2500/yr)", max_train_per_year = 2500)
toc()
c(n5000 = mean(aoa_s1$hist$in_aoa), n2500 = mean(aoa_s1_b$hist$in_aoa))

aoa_s1$threshold
aoa_s2$threshold

qs::qsave(aoa_s1, file.path(out_dir, glue("aoa_stage1_{flag}.qs")))
qs::qsave(aoa_s2, file.path(out_dir, glue("aoa_stage2_{flag}.qs")))


# ---- Step 6: summaries by year, with training-year benchmark ------------------------

di_all <- bind_rows(
  aoa_s1$bench %>% mutate(stage = "Stage 1", period = "training (leave-year-out)"),
  aoa_s1$hist  %>% mutate(stage = "Stage 1", period = "historical"),
  aoa_s2$bench %>% mutate(stage = "Stage 2", period = "training (leave-year-out)"),
  aoa_s2$hist  %>% mutate(stage = "Stage 2", period = "historical")
)

di_year <- di_all %>%
  group_by(stage, period, year) %>%
  summarise(pct_cells_in_aoa = 100 * mean(in_aoa),
            median_DI        = median(DI),
            .groups = "drop")
print(di_year, n = Inf)

thresholds <- tibble(stage = c("Stage 1", "Stage 2"),
                     threshold = c(aoa_s1$threshold, aoa_s2$threshold))

p_di <- ggplot(di_all, aes(factor(year), DI, fill = period)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.2, linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_hline(data = thresholds, aes(yintercept = threshold), linetype = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~stage, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_discrete(breaks = as.character(seq(1950, 2024, 10))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Dissimilarity index (DI)", fill = NULL,
       title = glue("{flag} industrial: DI by year (dashed = AOA threshold)")) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
p_di
ggsave(file.path(out_dir, glue("di_by_year_{flag}.png")), p_di, width = 10, height = 7)

# maps for selected years
grid <- read.csv(grid_path) %>% select(pixel_id, lon, lat)

p_map <- bind_rows(aoa_s1$hist %>% mutate(stage = "Stage 1"),
                   aoa_s2$hist %>% mutate(stage = "Stage 2")) %>%
  filter(year %in% c(1950, 1980, 2010)) %>%
  left_join(grid, by = "pixel_id") %>%
  ggplot(aes(lon, lat, fill = in_aoa)) +

p_map

# ---- Step 7: which predictors push rows outside? -------------------------------------

range_check <- function(res, label) {
  rng <- res$train_vals %>%
    summarise(across(all_of(res$vars), list(lo = min, hi = max))) %>%
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = c("var", ".value"), names_pattern = "(.*)_(lo|hi)$")

  res$hist_vals %>%
    mutate(decade = 10 * floor(year / 10)) %>%
    pivot_longer(all_of(res$vars), names_to = "var") %>%
    left_join(rng, by = "var") %>%
    group_by(var, decade) %>%
    summarise(pct_outside_range = round(100 * mean(value < lo | value > hi), 1), .groups = "drop") %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = decade, values_from = pct_outside_range) %>%
    mutate(stage = label, importance = round(res$weights[var], 1), .before = 1) %>%
    arrange(desc(importance))
}

range_check(aoa_s1, "Stage 1") %>% print(n = Inf)
range_check(aoa_s2, "Stage 2") %>% print(n = Inf)


# ---- Step 8: effort-weighted AOA (the headline number) -------------------------------

effort <- fread(effort_path) %>%
  filter(flag_country_iso3c == flag, year %in% hindcast_years) %>%   # edit column names to match your file
  left_join(global_grid %>%
              dplyr::select(-geometry_wkt)) %>%
  group_by(pixel_id, year) %>%
  summarise(effort = sum(nom_active_fishing_hours, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%   # edit effort column name
  filter(effort > 0)

# sanity checks: should both be 0
effort %>% anti_join(aoa_s1$hist, by = c("pixel_id", "year")) %>% nrow()
effort %>% anti_join(aoa_s2$hist, by = c("pixel_id", "year")) %>% nrow()

aoa_effort <- effort %>%
  left_join(aoa_s1$hist %>% select(pixel_id, year, in_s1 = in_aoa), by = c("pixel_id", "year")) %>%
  left_join(aoa_s2$hist %>% select(pixel_id, year, in_s2 = in_aoa), by = c("pixel_id", "year")) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(pct_effort_s1   = 100 * sum(effort[in_s1 %in% TRUE]) / sum(effort),
            pct_effort_s2   = 100 * sum(effort[in_s2 %in% TRUE]) / sum(effort),
            pct_effort_both = 100 * sum(effort[in_s1 %in% TRUE & in_s2 %in% TRUE]) / sum(effort),
            .groups = "drop")
print(aoa_effort, n = Inf)

# ---- Step 9: fleet composition (gear x length strata unseen in training) --------------

train_strata <- train_s2 %>%                    # strata with observed AIS effort
  distinct(gear, length_category) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.character), seen = TRUE)

strata_check <- qs::qread(here("data/int/rousseau_gear_fix.qs")) %>%
  filter(sector == "I", country == flag, year %in% hindcast_years) %>%
  group_by(year, gear = gear_new, length_category) %>%
  summarise(effort = sum(eff_active_hours, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(across(c(gear, length_category), as.character)) %>%
  left_join(train_strata, by = c("gear", "length_category"))

strata_check %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(pct_effort_unseen_strata = 100 * sum(effort[is.na(seen)]) / sum(effort)) %>%
  print(n = Inf)

strata_check %>% filter(is.na(seen)) %>% distinct(gear, length_category)   # which strata

# ---- Step 10: sensitivity to the year term --------------------------------------------
# Re-predict selected historical years with year set to different training years.
# High correlations => the (clamped) year term has little influence on the allocation.

year_sensitivity <- function(rf, pred_dir, flag, hist_years, set_years, stage) {
  map_dfr(hist_years, \(hy) {
    d <- read_full_pred_rows(pred_dir, flag, hy, hist_env)
    preds <- map(set_years, \(sy) {
      p <- predict(rf, data = mutate(d, year = sy), num.threads = 4)$predictions
      if (stage == 1) p[, "1"] else p
    })
    names(preds) <- paste0("y", set_years)
    as_tibble(preds) %>%
      summarise(across(-1, ~ cor(.x, preds[[1]], method = "spearman"))) %>%
      mutate(stage = stage, hist_year = hy, reference = names(preds)[1], .before = 1)
  })
}

bind_rows(
  year_sensitivity(rf_s1, stage_1_pred_dir, flag, c(1960, 1990), c(2015, 2019, 2024), 1),
  year_sensitivity(rf_s2, stage_2_pred_dir, flag, c(1960, 1990), c(2015, 2019, 2024), 2)
)
```

```{r}
## Ok, so what I think all of this is telling me is that the primary culprit is the MPA variables. It is likely these don't really add too much to the modelling anyways, so we should consider dropping them. And 2) re-do the bias correction. 


test_mpa <- hist_s1 %>% group_by(year) %>% summarise(median(nearest_mpa_distance_m)) # DI drops sharply in 1971 and 2004, corresponding with MPA designations near AUS fishing grounds. so MPA is pretty much the whole reason for the DI being high. 

# This is more than an AOA issue. In 2015–2024, nearly every cell is relatively close to some MPA. In 1950 there were hardly any, so distances are far larger than anything seen in training. A random forest can’t extrapolate, so every historical cell gets treated as though it sits at the most remote MPA distance in the training data. Those leaves were learned from very different places, such as mid-ocean cells. So the MPA variables may be feeding the historical predictions values with no meaning, and on this point the reviewer is right.

# I think the move is to just drop the MPA variables from the analysis. 1) they were included in the McDonald et al paper because that was an MPA analysis, and 2) pretty much all of the same spatial info is contained in lat/lon and distance from shore/ports variables.

# The predictor has no historical counterpart. MPAs were essentially absent before the 1970s, and most of today’s coverage dates from after 2000. For most of the hindcast period, “distance to nearest MPA” describes something that didn’t exist. That’s a problem with the variable for hindcasting, not something a tuning choice can fix.
# It belonged in McDonald et al. (2024) because of their question. They were estimating MPA effects on fishing within the AIS era. Your question is historical allocation, so the variable doesn’t carry over. Cite them for the framework and note this one departure.
# The AOA gives you evidence for the change. You aren’t dropping a variable on a hunch: the analysis showed it was the main source of extrapolation in predictor space.
# A distance cap would need its own justification. Spillover literature could support one, but a reviewer could still ask “why 100 km?”. Dropping the variables avoids that question.
```
